done.why: I ran out at the 150-turn limit. I had died in the Machine Room, woken up back in the barrow with nothing but the lamp, and was walking back through the carousel to get my things. My own count was a few turns under what the world said.

about: An underground realm haunted by a prankster wizard who pops in to cast spells on you that only half work. You walk down from a sealed barrow, past a ravine and a formal garden with a skittish unicorn, into a spinning carousel room that throws you out a random exit. Past that are a riddle door, a magic well you ride up in a bucket, a mad tea party with cakes, and a robot that waits for orders. It's a place of tricks and illusions where the scenery has been described with care.

moments.note: Examining the moss brought the Wizard in to cast 'Fear!', and I fled onto the foot bridge.
Going southeast got cut off by fear of the Wizard and I ran off to the gazebo. There was a typo too: 'There's is a Wizard'.
The place mat is 'thin enough to slide under most doors, should you ever need to'. A nice quiet hint.
The 'Fantasize!' spell put an illusory bulging chest in the room, and it wasn't there when I tried to open it. Clever.
The unicorn ran off, 'unsurprised by this evidence that you are indeed the uncouth sort of vagabond it suspected you were'.
The ledge west of the Deep Ford is blocked off with 'will have to wait'. Several carousel exits were also rockfalls.
The Wizard tried 'Fall!', nothing happened, and he left looking embarrassed.
Answering 'a well' to the riddle got a hollow laugh. Only 'say well' opened the door.
The 'Ferment!' spell made me drunk and I stumbled into the wrong rooms. Funny, though it got tiring.
I poured the teapot water into the bucket and rose to the top of the well: 'Well done.'
I pushed the round button despite the HIGH VOLTAGE sign and was fried. A mysterious face sent me back to the barrow and my things were gone. That was my own fault.
The walk back through the random carousel took up my last turns.

wished: Take several things at once, like 'take all from table' or 'take all cakes'
Answer the riddle in the form I typed first ('answer "a well"')
Get past the ledge and the rockfall passages that 'will have to wait'
Find a way to win the unicorn's trust and get its key
Find out what the robot could do and what the cakes did, before I ran out of turns

lines.line: It has that look of a thing that has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
lines.why: It set a warm, knowing tone from the very first object.

lines.line: thin enough to slide under most doors, should you ever need to slide something under a door.
lines.why: A hint worked into a description without fuss.

lines.line: The unicorn, unsurprised by this evidence that you are indeed the uncouth sort of vagabond it suspected you were, melts into the hedges and is gone.
With a slightly embarrassed glance in your direction, he vanishes.
lines.why: It made the Wizard likeable instead of only annoying.

lines.line: You are at the top of the well. Well done.
lines.why: A pun as the payoff for my first real puzzle.

lines.line: Perhaps you may be of some use to me in gaining my freedom from this place.
lines.why: A hint at a bigger story behind dying.

fun.why: The Wizard's random spells, the illusions and the well puzzle were real fun. Dying and the carousel trudge took some shine off at the end.

engagement.why: Every new area (the riddle, the well, the tea room, the robot) pulled me on. I was eager to keep going when I hit the cap.

difficulty.why: The puzzles were fair and mostly hinted, like the bucket and water. The riddle phrasing and the random carousel added friction, and the death was a reasonable punishment.

interestingness.why: A world with personality: a wizard who meddles, things that may be illusions, topiary that shifts. Some areas are deliberately closed off with 'will have to wait'.

prose.why: The examine text is consistently witty and specific, from the lantern to the shadows to the bucket. One typo at turn 22.
